intent: Render the transient notifications a toast manager holds, stacked in a fixed region over the page.
typical_uses: Mounted once near the application root, showing every toast fired through the shared `toast` manager
A second, isolated notification region bound to its own `createToastManager()` manager

dont_use_when.situation: A status message that belongs to the current page and stays in its flow
A message the user must acknowledge or decide on before continuing
A validation message tied to one form control

invariants.text: A toast is shown by calling `add` (or `promise`) on the manager Toaster is bound to; the kit exports no toast part to compose as JSX, and each card's title, description, type icon and action come from the toast object passed to `add`; every card also carries a close button named by `closeLabel`.
The notification region portals into `container`, or the document body without one, wherever Toaster sits in the tree; its children are rendered in place.
Without `toastManager`, Toaster renders the shared `toast` manager's toasts; two Toasters bound to the same manager each render every toast, once per region.
The manager keeps no queue: a toast added while no Toaster bound to that manager is mounted is dropped silently and never appears.

anti_patterns.dont: Mount a Toaster in each fragment of a composed application on the shared manager
anti_patterns.do_instead: Mount one Toaster for the shared `toast` manager, and give any extra region its own `createToastManager()` manager

anti_patterns.dont: Leave `label` and `closeLabel` at their English defaults in a non-English application
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass translated `label` (the region's accessible name) and `closeLabel` (each close button's accessible name)

a11y.by: The primitive's Toast.Viewport (role="region", aria-live="polite") and Toast.Root (role="dialog", or "alertdialog" for a toast with `priority: 'high'`, labelled by its title and described by its description), plus toast.test.tsx, which asserts the region's accessible name ("Notifications" by default, replaced by `label`), the dialog role of each card and the close button's accessible name ("Close toast" by default, replaced by `closeLabel`)

children.states: children is any React content, rendered in place; any depth of it can read the manager through useToastManager
children.because: `React.ReactNode` is a union of elements, strings, numbers, fragments and more; the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

container.states: container is the node the notification region portals into, the document body when absent
container.because: Base UI types it `HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | null` or a React ref object holding one, and the compiler emits one JSON type per property. Passing a themed subtree's node makes the toasts inherit that subtree's tokens.

toastManager.states: toastManager is the manager object whose toasts this Toaster renders, the shared `toast` manager when absent
toastManager.because: A manager is an object of functions (`add`, `close`, `update`, `promise` and a `' subscribe'` function) returned by `createToastManager()`; no JSON Schema type covers a function.

unexposed_parts.reason: Toaster renders it around its children, bound to `toastManager`.
The portalled notification region, named by `label`, that holds the toast cards.

unexposed_parts.part: Toast.Root, Toast.Content, Toast.Title, Toast.Description, Toast.Action and Toast.Close
unexposed_parts.reason: One card per toast in the manager, laid out by the kit and filled from the toast object; the close button is named by `closeLabel` and the action button is rendered only when the toast carries `actionProps`.

good.title: One Toaster at the root, toasts fired from anywhere
good.code:
<Toaster label="Notifications" closeLabel="Close notification">
  <App />
</Toaster>

toast.add({ type: 'success', title: 'Saved', description: 'Your changes have been saved.' });

good.title: An isolated region with its own manager

bad.title: Composing a toast as JSX
bad.why: The kit exports no Toast component; a toast is shown with `toast.add({ title: 'Saved' })` and rendered by the mounted Toaster.

companions.description: The shared manager every Toaster renders by default. `toast.add({ title, description, type, actionProps })` shows a toast and returns its id; `close` and `update` act on a toast already shown, by its id; `promise(promise, { loading, success, error })` shows a loading toast for the promise and updates it to a success or an error toast when the promise settles. It can be called from anywhere, without a hook or a Toaster ancestor.
Creates a manager independent of the shared `toast`, for a Toaster passed it as `toastManager`.

Reads the live toast list and the `add`, `close`, `update` and `promise` of the nearest Toaster's manager; it throws when called with no Toaster above it. It does not render toasts: the kit exports no toast parts to render them with.

cannot_extract: default: prop "toastManager" defaults to "toast", which is not a literal - the body gives no single literal default for it
